newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - FEB 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - FEB 28.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The coalition conference reached an agreement yesterday about deregulation of electricity and gas prices and rents, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus. The cabinet will clarify the price increase next Wednesday. Rents should increase this year on average by 50 percent, and electricity and gas prices will probably increase by 35 percent.

- The Defence Ministry lost part of its paperwork important for entry into NATO. The documents contain all the information about what the Army must do in order to be ready for cooperation with NATO troops. The ministry will attempt to find the papers, but may have to ask for them again from Brussels.

PRAVO - On Thursday, parliament voted in favour of lifting the immunity of the head of the Republican party (SPR-RSC), Miroslav Sladek, and two other representatives of the party, Josef Krejsa and Ruldolf Smucer, and all three may be criminally prosecuted. SPR-RSC plans to boycott parliament meetings in protest.
- The administrative council of Czech Railways met on Thursday and decided not to remove the general director, Rudolf Mladek, from his position.

- Along with the approval of the deregulation law yesterday, parliament decided that citizens with incomes less than 1.6 times the minimum will receive social aid to help them pay the new prices. After July, families with 1.4 times the minimum can also receive aid.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Marko Stehlik, the director of Poldi Steel, announced that workers' wages up to last November will be paid today, and employees who worked this January will also receive a deposit for further wages next week.
- On February 21, the 10th issue of shares of Banka Hana was completed, and the bank increased its basic capital by 900 million crowns to a total of 2.7 billion crowns.
- Parliament approved a law for state businesses yesterday, which should create a legal foundation for economic operations within businesses which are not yet to be fully privatised.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Membership in NATO for the Czech Republic and Poland is financially more advantageous than neutrality. Chairman of Parliament Milos Zeman and Polish Defence Minister Stanislaw Dobrzanski agreed on this yesterday in Prague, and Dobrzanski discussed the possibility that Poland and the Czech Republic would enter into the alliance together in 1999.
- Parliament approved a law yesterday freezing all financial operations directly and indirectly connected with Libyan capital, exept transactions concerning oil.
